items.text: Calm, unhurried footsteps emerge from the courtyard.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Seems they've had martial arts training.
The guards hastily make way, their voices softening with deference.

items.speaker: Stern Guard
items.text: D-Doctor Xiù, have you finished examining Master Hú?

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: You mean his night blindness? Exactly how much time do you expect me to waste on that man?

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: And you, out here making a racket and swinging your weapons about while I'm trying to write a prescription!

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Care to explain yourselves? Hm?
She takes the steps two at a time, passing Chéng without so much as a glance.
The villagers all lower their weapons, allowing her to approach the gravely injured man. She narrows her eyes as she examines him.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: How did this happen?

items.speaker: Disheartened Villager
items.text: We were hunting in the mountains and ran into a tiger. My brother, he fell behind and—
Before he can finish, Doctor Xiù turns and strides back toward the gate.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Get him in here!

items.speaker: Stern Guard
items.text: But Doctor Xiù! He's covered in blood! How could we possibly carry him into Master Hú's courtyard?!

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: It's bad luck for someone to die at the gate, is it not? I'll ask Master Hú for a room myself!
She pauses, then turns back impatiently.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Well? Unless you wish for this man to die, I suggest you bring him in!

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: Ah, r-right.

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: Quickly, let's get him inside!
Two villagers rush the wounded man inside, streaking the entrance steps with blood as they ascend.

items.speaker: Cowardly Guard
items.text: Should we wipe it up? If it dries, it'll be harder to clean.

items.speaker: Stern Guard
items.text: Of course, you dolt! Unless you're looking for a scolding, you'll wipe it this instant!
The guards fetch water from the courtyard and begin hurriedly scrubbing Master Hú's steps.

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: Hmph. Despicable!

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: All's well that ends well, it seems.
Chéng is just about to leave when the lead villager steps in to block his path.

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: Wait.

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: Who are you? Why did you cut down my arrow?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Only a passing traveler. Your arrow would never have pierced that guard's rattan shield, but it would have given them a reason to retaliate.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Your recklessness will cause nothing but trouble.

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: I may have lost my temper, but I've put up with them and their shoddy treatment for far too long to care about the consequences! If they fight, then we fight!

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: And if you'd made the first move, you'd have been deemed the primary culprit. Were someone to die, your punishment would be death.

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: And what of it?! You think I fear death?! Hah!

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: The way you speak—it's obvious you come from noble stock. How could someone like you understand our struggles?
The disjointed back-and-forth frays Chéng's patience.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I'm not—
During their exchange, several village guards rush over, stirring up a cloud of yellow dust under the Paifang.

items.speaker: Headman
items.text: What's going on here?!
Master Hú's personal guards hurry forward to greet them, directing their accusations at the villagers sitting cross-legged by the gate.

items.speaker: Stern Guard
items.text: It's these troublemakers! They've dirtied Master Hú's steps!

items.speaker: Calm Villager
items.text: We didn't mean to cause trouble. Someone was mauled by a tiger and urgently needed treatment!

items.speaker: Headman
items.text: Another tiger attack? We've lost three people this month to those beasts!

items.speaker: Headman
items.text: We have warned you over and over not to travel into the mountains. Why go up there?

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: With this year's feeble harvest, what choice did we have? Five years ago it was floods, and now it's drought! Grain has grown more expensive than gold!

items.speaker: Lead Villager
items.text: If we don't hunt, what are we to eat?

items.speaker: Calm Villager
items.text: My land has all been taken, and we have no grain stored for the winter. Hunting rabbits is the only way we can scrape together a half-decent meal.

items.speaker: Disheartened Villager
items.text: If only ... If only an immortal would appear again, as they did five years ago, handing out grain to us all.
After a moment's hesitation, Chéng steps past the village guards and offers the headman a modest bow.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I've had some formal weapons training, including hand-to-hand. If you aim to head into the mountains to hunt the tiger, I will offer my assistance.
The village guards exchange amused glances.

items.speaker: Headman
items.text: That mountain forest isn't meant for travel. Only a fool would go there without a good reason. Had these hunters not been so greedy, this wouldn't have happened.

items.speaker: Headman
items.text: The tiger attacked them in the forest, not the village. We can't go traipsing into the forest hunting tigers. We'd never get any real work done!
With a dismissive wave, he turns back to scold the grime-covered villagers.

items.speaker: Headman
items.text: That's enough! Go back to your homes! And no one is to go up the mountain again!

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Your decree doesn't change the fact that these hunters still have families to feed.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: That tiger has taken too many lives. It cannot be ignored.
The headman suddenly swings his staff as if he were swatting at an annoying mosquito. Its tip brushes inches from the hem of Chéng's clothes.

items.speaker: Headman
items.text: You're getting on my last nerve, boy!

items.speaker: Headman
items.text: You are neither an official nor a member of this village. What good does it serve you to stick your nose into our business?

items.speaker: Headman
items.text: If you're so eager to play the hero, go deal with the tiger yourself.
Broken cries echo from the courtyard. Chéng tightens his grip on the hilt of his blade.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: This is absurd.
He pushes past the guards, once again placing himself between them and the villagers.

items.speaker: Headman
items.text: Hey! What do you think you're doing?!

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: The tiger. Can you tell me exactly where you encountered it?
Mountaintop, Riverside Village

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Enter the forest and head due south. After passing another slope, it is somewhere near the edge of the cliff.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: They said the tiger is blue and white, two or three times larger than an ordinary one. It almost sounds like a monster.
Ahead stretches a thick pine forest with shrubs reaching up to the knee. Wild grass lies flattened in the undergrowth, streaked with dull, rust-red blood.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: This is where the hunter was wounded. I should proceed with caution.
The forest wind falls silent, and the wild grass rustles softly.
The sound of heavy breathing reaches Chéng's ears.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: It's sneaked behind me!
A massive tiger, blue streaks in its magnificent white fur, bursts from the grass, slamming Chéng to the ground.
He braces his half-drawn blade across his chest, barely holding off the attack.
Blue flames flare across the tiger's brow as it presses its claws against the blade.

items.speaker: Tiger
items.text: *roar*

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: That's some strength, hah!
A feather shoots from his shoulder guard like an arrow, piercing the tiger's forehead.

items.speaker: Tiger
items.text: Graaargh!
A thunderous roar shakes the forest. In an attempt to escape, the tiger clamps its jaws around Chéng's blade and hauls him forward.
Chéng refuses to let go as the tiger barrels forward, rushing them both to a nearby cliff edge.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: No!
As the tiger leaps, a sudden sense of weightlessness comes over Chéng.
In a split second, he grabs hold of the cliff edge, his body dangling below.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Urgh!
One, two, three ... Feather after feather pierces downward.
With the final impact, the tiger's grip loosens. It lets out a final howl as it plummets down into the ravine below and vanishes out of sight.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Phew!

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: The soil is too loose. It needs to be harder if I'm to pull myself up.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Breathe. Sense the flow of Qi. Wherever it touches, the earth hardens like iron.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Concentrate ...
The soil beneath his fingers takes on a faint metallic sheen but doesn't spread any further.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Is it too much for me to handle?
As the soil's binding begins to fail, the clump in his grip begins to break apart.
A pale fog blankets the foot of the cliff. Falling would surely mean his demise.
Even so, he feels his grip beginning to falter.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Darn it!
A heartbeat before his fingers give out, a thin silver thread slices through the air from the cliff edge.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: That's—!
